newsitem.title: UK: Stg/mark off lows after stumble on George comments.
newsitem.headline: Stg/mark off lows after stumble on George comments.

text.p: Sterling/mark dived nearly two pfennigs to below 2.82 marks at midday in Europe after Bank of England Governor Eddie George said there was "exaggerated strength" in the pound's exchange rate.

But the pound, which hit a fresh four-and-a-half year high of 2.8331 marks earlier, was likely to pick up steam after its brief dip and head higher on expectations of an interest rate rise after the UK May purchasing managers' index (PMI) showed a surging service sector, analysts said.
At 1145 GMT sterling/mark was trading at 2.8175/85 against 2.8250/60 in late Europe on Tuesday. Cable was at $1.6272/85 against $1.6348/58.

Britain's new monetary policy committee meets for the first time on Friday and the largest rise yet in the PMI service of business activity to 64.8, compared to 61.2 in April, is likely to have strengthened its resolve to tighten policy.

"Eddie George is going to want to make his mark as soon as possible, and he's going to practise that by hiking rates at the first opportunity," said David Brown, chief European economist at Bear Sterns here.
A Reuters poll of analysts expectations' forecast a rise in UK interest rates of 0.25 percent when the monetary committee meets on Friday, taking the rate to 6.50 percent.
And the prospect of this should carry sterling/mark higher.

"It may be that he (George) is taking some of the steam out of sterling while suggesting an interest rate rise on Friday," said Mark Miller, UK economist at Morgan Stanley. "I think you can expect to see sterling/mark tick a little higher."
He said the session high of 2.8331 could be revisited before the close of trade.
And sterling/mark would also be driven higher by ongoing worries about a soft euro, as the fued in Germany over the revaluation of the Bundesbank's gold reserves continues.
"A strong dollar will provide a strong impetus for the pound," said Brown.
